titulo: Latent Information Reconstruction via Vector Divergence in Market Microstructure
resumen: Quantitative finance models treat microstructure data (order books, trade flows) and public data (news, market sentiment) as independent sources. This separation fails to capture a welldocumented phenomenon: markets regularly price in information before it becomes publicly available. This paper proposes a methodology based on vector divergence between these two streams. By projecting order book state and public narrative consensus into a shared vector space, we define a metric D(t) that measures the gap between market behavior and public information in real time. A sharp increase in D(t) signals an active informational gap between market behavior and public consensus. The architecture combines a microstructural encoder, a semantic encoder (NLP) and a vector database for storage, historical precedent search and realtime inference. It builds on Bouchaud's work on market endogeneity and on Hawkes processes for noise filtering. We validate the approach on two real events, GameStop (January 2021) and Terra/LUNA (May 2022). In both cases, the divergence proxy crosses the detection threshold 36 to 48 hours before extreme price movements of 9.4 and 13.1 standard deviations respectively, confirming that latent information was present in the microstructure (or its on-chain equivalent) but absent from public consensus.
